name: Newark Museum of Art
unique: A encyclopedic museum with one of the best Tibetan collections in the west, a Victorian ballroom and a planetarium, in a city most visitors skip.
buzz: The Tibetan galleries are the reason curators come; the Ballantine House next door is a separate tour and the planetarium is cheap.

name: Thomas Edison National Historical Park
unique: Edison's three story laboratory complex with 400,000 artifacts, a machine shop that could build anything and a recording studio where the first sound was captured.
buzz: The chemistry lab and the machine shop are the best preserved; the ranger tour of the main building is worth timing your visit for.

name: Liberty State Park
unique: The old Central Railroad terminal on the harbor with the Empty Sky memorial, a 30 acre lawn and the ferry dock for the Statue of Liberty.
buzz: The memorial and the skyline view are the draw; the ferry leaves from here and parking is far cheaper than Manhattan.

name: Loew's Jersey Theatre
customer: Movie palace fans, architecture people, film lovers
unique: A 3,200 seat 1929 movie palace with a ceiling of gilded stars and clouds, saved by volunteers and still showing classic films on 35mm.
buzz: The restoration is the story and volunteers run tours; film fans say the balcony seats are the best in the state.

name: Fort Lee Historic Park
unique: The bluff where Washington's army built a fort to block the Hudson, with reconstructed huts and a cliff edge view of the George Washington Bridge.
buzz: The view is the reason to stop and the history is the bonus; the cliff trail below is a separate walk with real exposure.

name: Tenafly Nature Center
unique: Four hundred acres of deciduous forest and a lake with a resident barred owl and a trail system that feels remote for being 15 minutes from the George Washington Bridge.
buzz: The owl and the pond are the easy wins with children; trails are flat and the center runs weekend programs.

name: Paterson Great Falls
unique: A 77 foot waterfall in the middle of a city where Alexander Hamilton planned the first industrial city, with raceways, mills and a hydroelectric plant still running.
buzz: The falls from the bridge are the photo and the ranger walk explains the engineering; the surrounding blocks are rough and the park is well patrolled.

name: Ringwood Manor
customer: House tour people, history fans, gardeners
unique: A 51 room ironmaster's mansion in the Ramapo hills with period rooms, a walled garden and the forges and mines that armed the Revolution nearby.
buzz: The house tour is the only way in and the guides know the families; the state park trails behind it are free and quiet.

name: Morristown National Historical Park
customer: History families, hikers, rev war people
unique: The winter encampment where the Continental Army survived 1779, with Washington's Ford Mansion, reconstructed log huts and 27 miles of trails through Jockey Hollow.
buzz: The huts and the Wick House are the walk and the mansion tour is separate; the park is the first national historical park in the country.

name: Historic Speedwell
unique: The ironworks village where Samuel Morse demonstrated the telegraph in 1838, with the original factory building, a wheelwright shop and a working letterpress.
buzz: The telegraph story is the hook and the volunteers demonstrate it; the site is small and best combined with Jockey Hollow.

name: Duke Farms
unique: A 2,700 acre estate with nine lakes, a 1909 conservatory, a hay barn cafe and miles of paved paths where bicycles are free to borrow.
buzz: The free bike borrow and the orchid range are the local secret; it is the former Doris Duke estate and the trails are flat.

name: Leonard J. Buck Garden
unique: A rock garden built into a wooded ravine with a stream, ponds and paths that switchback through alpine plants, hidden behind a suburban office park.
buzz: Gardeners call it the best small garden in the state; spring is the peak and the paths are steep and narrow.

name: Watchung Reservation
unique: Two thousand acres of forest with a lake, a nature center and the Deserted Village of Feltville, an 1840s mill town abandoned and still standing in the woods.
buzz: The deserted village is the strange draw and the lake trail is the easy walk; the nature center has live animals for children.

name: Miller-Cory House
unique: A 1740 farmhouse where volunteers cook over the open hearth and work the garden with 18th century tools on Sunday afternoons.
buzz: The open hearth cooking is the reason to time a visit; it is run by volunteers and small enough to feel like a neighbor's house.

name: Thomas Edison Center at Menlo Park
company: Thomas Alva Edison Memorial Tower Corporation
customer: Science people, families, local history fans
unique: A 131 foot Art Deco tower of Edison's light bulb on the site of his Menlo Park lab, with a small museum of phonographs and early bulbs.
buzz: The tower is visible from the highway and the museum is one room; locals bring visiting engineers and the ranger talk is good.

name: Delaware and Raritan Canal State Park
unique: Seventy miles of towpath along an 1830s canal, flat and gravel, with a mule drawn boat at Griggstown and herons the whole way.
buzz: The Princeton to Kingston stretch is the standard ride; the path is flat and shaded and the canal is stocked with fish.

name: Red Mill Museum Village
unique: A red painted gristmill on the South Branch with a limestone quarry, a one room schoolhouse and a mule drawn canal boat, all in a village of 2,700 people.
buzz: The mill and the quarry are the tour and the bridge over the river is the photograph; check hours before driving, it is seasonal.

name: Delaware River Tubing
unique: A three mile float down the Delaware between wooded New Jersey and Pennsylvania banks, with small rapids, rope swings and a bus back to the start.
buzz: Bring water shoes and a dry bag; the river is shallow in August and the weekend crowds are loud by noon.

name: WheatonArts
unique: The Museum of American Glass with 7,000 pieces, a working glass studio where you can watch a gather and blow, and a folk art center on a wooded campus.
buzz: Glassblowing demos run all day and the paperweight collection is the surprise; in April the glass festival fills the grounds.

name: East Point Lighthouse
unique: A brick 1849 lighthouse at the mouth of the Maurice River, surrounded by marsh and one of the best shorebird staging areas on the Delaware Bay.
buzz: In May the horseshoe crabs and red knots draw birders from other countries; the lighthouse opens on select weekends and the road is gravel.

name: Red Bank Battlefield
unique: The bluff above the Delaware where a 1777 fort held off a Hessian attack, with earthworks, the Whitall House and a view across to Philadelphia International.
buzz: The archaeology dig that found soldiers' remains made news; the park is free and the river path is a good evening walk.

name: William Heritage Winery
unique: A family fruit farm that turned to wine, with a tasting room over the vineyard and peach and apple orchards that pick in summer.
buzz: The dry riesling and the cider are the orders; the deck is the reason to come on a fall afternoon.

name: Cowtown Rodeo
unique: The oldest weekly professional rodeo in the country, running Saturday nights in a South Jersey field with bull riding, barrel racing and a calf scramble for children.
buzz: Locals bring blankets to the bleachers and first timers are surprised by how fast the night goes; the funnel cake stand is the tradition.

name: Fort Mott State Park
unique: An 1890s harbor defense fort on the Delaware with concrete batteries you can walk through, a ferry to a island fort and a river beach.
buzz: The batteries are open and dark and children love them; the ferry to Pea Patch Island and Fort Delaware runs in summer.

name: Battleship New Jersey
unique: The most decorated battleship in American history, with a 16 inch gun turret you can climb inside, a guided engine room tour and the captain's cabin.
buzz: The turret climb is the thing people remember; the engine room tour costs extra and is worth it, and the deck view of Philadelphia is free.

name: Adventure Aquarium
unique: A shark tunnel you walk under, a hippo exhibit with underwater viewing and a touch tank of stingrays, on the Camden waterfront across from Philadelphia.
buzz: The hippos and the shark tunnel are the hits; tickets are cheaper online and the garage is the easiest parking.

name: Cape May Lighthouse
unique: A 1859 brick tower with 199 steps and a view over the Cape May point where two bays meet, inside a state park that is a major migration stop.
buzz: The climb is worth the view and the fall hawk watch at the park is a separate draw; the beach below is free.

name: Twin Lights
unique: Twin granite towers on the Navesink Highlands with a museum in one and a view of the Atlantic and New York Harbor from the other.
buzz: The view from the north tower is the best on the Jersey shore; the museum covers the Marconi wireless station that once stood here.

name: Island Beach State Park
unique: Ten miles of undeveloped barrier beach with dunes, a maritime forest and no boardwalk, between the ocean and Barnegat Bay.
buzz: The park closes when the lot fills, usually by nine in summer; the bay side is calm for children and the trails are empty in September.

name: Batsto Village
unique: A bog iron and glassmaking village in the Pine Barrens with a mansion, a sawmill, a gristmill and worker cottages, abandoned when the iron ran out.
buzz: The village is free to walk and the mansion tour is cheap; the pond and the pine woods make it a good half day.
